hardinessNote: 5 to 10°C; frost-tender. Protect from UK winter frost.
visual: Architectural evergreen subshrub with silvery-grey, hairy leaves and spectacular upright spikes packed with violet-blue flowers.
soilWarning: Winter wet and frost kill it; no heavy soil
water: Water while establishing; once established, water sparingly outdoors. Reduce watering markedly in winter.
prune: Remove spent flowering spikes and damaged growth; avoid cutting deeply into old wood.
toxicity: Coarse hairs can irritate skin; wear gloves when handling.
cvs: Echium fastuosum is widely used in horticulture but is treated by RHS as a misapplied name for Echium candicans.
resilience: Good drought and coastal tolerance; very poor frost tolerance. Pests: slugs on young growth; whitefly and spider mites under glass.
uses: Mediterranean borders, coastal gardens, pollinator planting, architectural displays, large containers
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; attractive to bees and other nectar-feeding insects.

hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; shelter from cold winds and severe winter exposure.
visual: Dense evergreen shrub with small glossy dark-green leaves and masses of brilliant indigo-blue flower clusters in spring.
soilWarning: No waterlogging, wet clay or frost pockets
water: Water regularly while establishing; drought-tolerant once established.
prune: Lightly trim immediately after flowering; avoid cutting into old, leafless wood.
cvs: Synonym: Ceanothus impressus 'Victoria'. Keep separate from the species Ceanothus impressus.
resilience: Drought-tolerant once established; suitable for mild coastal gardens. Pests: scale insects.
uses: Flowering borders, informal hedges, sheltered walls, wildlife gardens, coastal gardens
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; spring flowers provide nectar and pollen for bees.

hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; requires good drainage and protection from cold winds.
visual: Broad, spreading evergreen shrub with tiny dark-green leaves and abundant rounded clusters of deep blue spring flowers.
water: Water during establishment; thereafter water mainly during prolonged drought.
prune: Lightly shape after flowering; do not prune hard into bare old wood.
cvs: Species record; do not merge with Ceanothus 'Victoria'.
resilience: Good drought tolerance and suitability for mild coastal conditions. Pests: scale insects.
uses: Spreading shrub borders, sunny banks, wildlife planting, gravel gardens, Mediterranean planting
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; flowers are attractive to bees and other pollinating insects.

hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; protect against severe frost and cold, drying winds.
visual: Compact rounded evergreen with slender aromatic dark-green leaflets and abundant fragrant white star-shaped flowers, often reblooming in late summer.
soilWarning: Avoid cold waterlogged ground and exposure
water: Water regularly while establishing and during extended dry spells; avoid persistent saturation.
prune: Lightly trim after spring flowering to maintain a rounded habit; remove damaged stems.
toxicity: Aromatic foliage may irritate sensitive skin; no other hazard known.
cvs: WHITE DAZZLER is the trade designation; 'Londaz' is the cultivar denomination.
resilience: Good tolerance of coastal conditions and summer drought after establishment. Pests: scale insects, spider mites and snails.
uses: Small gardens, evergreen borders, low informal hedging, fragrant planting, patio containers
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; fragrant flowers attract bees and other insects.

hardinessNote: -20 to -15°C; very cold-hardy, though exposed container roots need protection.
visual: Compact deciduous hydrangea with large cone-shaped blooms opening lime green, transitioning through cream and pink to rich reddish-pink.
soilWarning: No drought in sun; deep shade cuts flowers
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth and flowering; water containers frequently in summer.
prune: Cut back in late winter or early spring to encourage strong new shoots and large flower panicles.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten by dogs and cats; may cause skin irritation.
cvs: LITTLE LIME PUNCH is the trade name for cultivar 'SMNHPH'; distinct from LITTLE LIME ('Jane').
resilience: Very good winter hardiness; flowers reliably on current-season growth. Pests: aphids, capsid bugs and hydrangea scale.
uses: Patio containers, small gardens, mixed borders, low flowering hedges, cut flowers
pollination: not applicable; fertile florets may attract pollinators; showy sterile florets provide most of the display.
uncertain: Input interpreted as Little Lime Punch rather than Little Lime; verify the original label if possible.
H6 is supported by UK nursery information; RHS does not currently provide a full cultivar-specific hardiness assessment.

hardinessNote: -15 to -10°C; established plants may tolerate lower temperatures in sheltered positions.
visual: Compact evergreen azalea with glossy green leaves edged creamy white, often bronze-tinged in cold weather, and bright rose-pink to reddish-pink spring flowers.
soilWarning: No chalk or lime; no drought or waterlogging
water: Maintain consistent moisture, ideally using rainwater where tap water is hard.
prune: Remove dead branches and lightly shape immediately after flowering.
toxicity: Rhododendron foliage and flowers are harmful if eaten by people and pets.
cvs: Japanese evergreen azalea 'Silver Sword'; 'Variegata' is treated as a foliage descriptor, not part of the confirmed cultivar name.
resilience: Good cold tolerance when established; vulnerable to drought and alkaline growing conditions. Pests: vine weevil, lace bugs and leafhoppers.
uses: Ericaceous borders, woodland edges, Japanese gardens, containers, low evergreen planting
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; spring flowers can attract bees.
uncertain: The supplied name combines Silver Sword and Variegata. Silver Sword is a documented variegated cultivar, but verify the label to exclude a different cultivar.
H5 is a practical UK estimate rather than a verified cultivar-specific RHS assessment.

hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; may lose foliage in severe winter conditions.
visual: Neat evergreen clumps of fine arching, creamy-yellow leaves edged dark green, forming a softly cascading ornamental sedge.
soilWarning: Avoid drought and scorching afternoon sun
water: Maintain moderate, regular moisture; increase watering in sunny containers.
prune: Comb out or trim dead foliage in spring; avoid unnecessarily cutting the whole evergreen clump.
cvs: 'Jenneke' is a variegated selection of Carex brunnea.
resilience: Tolerates relatively damp soils; foliage may become semi-evergreen after severe frost. Pests: aphids.
uses: Edging, shaded containers, ground cover, courtyard planting, foliage combinations
pollination: not applicable; wind-pollinated; insignificant brownish flower spikes.

hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; shelter plants in cold or exposed gardens.
visual: Compact evergreen hellebore with distinctive silvery-grey, marbled leaves and outward-facing pale green flowers, sometimes delicately flushed pink.
soilWarning: No winter wet, root disturbance or acid soil
water: Water during establishment and prolonged drought; avoid waterlogged winter conditions.
prune: Remove damaged leaves and spent flowering stems after flowering; retain healthy evergreen foliage.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; sap may irritate skin. Toxic to pets.
cvs: 'Silver Star' is a named selection of Helleborus × sternii, a hybrid of H. argutifolius and H. lividus.
resilience: Moderate drought tolerance once established; requires reasonable drainage and shelter from severe winter weather. Pests: aphids, slugs and snails.
uses: Winter borders, courtyard gardens, containers, woodland edges, evergreen foliage displays
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; early flowers can provide food for bees during mild winter weather.
uncertain: Exact mature dimensions are approximate for Silver Star.
Hardiness follows breeder information and the RHS rating for Helleborus × sternii rather than an RHS cultivar-specific assessment.

hardinessNote: -20 to -15°C according to RHS; free drainage remains particularly important in winter.
visual: Compact, arching evergreen grass-like perennial with brilliant golden-yellow, narrow strap-shaped leaves cascading into a fountain-shaped mound.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and heavy, wet clay
water: Water regularly when newly planted; reduce watering once established, allowing the surface to dry between applications.
prune: Remove old or damaged leaves as necessary; no regular hard pruning required.
cvs: MINER'S GOLD is the trade designation for cultivar 'KM-MG24'.
resilience: Excellent drought tolerance after establishment; suitable for open and coastal planting. Pests: aphids, scale insects and mealybugs.
uses: Golden foliage accents, low borders, containers, mass planting, drought-tolerant gardens
pollination: not applicable; small flowers are of limited ornamental significance; pollination is not the primary garden interest.

common: Magical Lemon and Lime Heavenly Bamboo
latin: Nandina domestica MAGICAL LEMON AND LIME ('Lemlim')
hardinessNote: -10 to -5°C; shelter from severe cold winds.
visual: Compact, upright evergreen shrub with striking yellow-green new foliage maturing to fresh lime green, creating a bright, layered foliage display.
soilWarning: Avoid winter wet and drought in containers
water: Water regularly during establishment and dry weather; mature plants tolerate occasional drought.
prune: Minimal pruning required; remove individual old stems at their base in spring where necessary.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; particularly important around dogs and poultry.
cvs: MAGICAL LEMON AND LIME is the trade designation for cultivar 'Lemlim'; also sold as Lemon-Lime.
resilience: Good tolerance of summer heat and moderate drought after establishment.
uses: Evergreen borders, patio containers, small gardens, contrasting foliage displays, low-maintenance planting
pollination: not applicable; occasional summer flowers may be insect-pollinated; this cultivar is grown chiefly for foliage.

hardinessNote: -15 to -10°C; hardy in most UK gardens.
visual: Vigorous twining climber bearing strongly fragrant tubular flowers, deep rose-pink outside and glowing golden-orange within, against dark green foliage.
soilWarning: Avoid dry roots; stress brings aphids
water: Keep roots evenly moist during establishment and flowering; mulch annually.
prune: Prune after flowering to control size and remove tangled growth; renovate in late winter if required.
toxicity: Ornamental berries are not edible; keep away from children and pets.
cvs: Often sold as 'Goldflame'; RHS records the cultivar as 'Gold Flame'.
resilience: Strong growth and good winter hardiness; flowers best when roots remain cool and moist. Pests: honeysuckle aphids, thrips and whitefly.
uses: Pergolas, arches, trellises, boundary screens, wildlife gardens, fragrant seating areas
pollination: not applicable; insect-pollinated; nectar-rich flowers attract bees, butterflies and night-flying moths.
uncertain: Foliage may be fully deciduous in colder winters.
